claim_checks.value: A 13-page IEEE-format research paper documenting a structural vulnerability in WebRTC-based exam proctoring. Operating systems expose documented APIs, SetWindowDisplayAffinity on Windows and NSWindow.SharingType.none on macOS, that let an application exclude its window from tested screen-capture paths while remaining fully visible on the physical display. This challenges the trust assumption in capture-based proctoring. Proof-of-concept implementations achieved 100% evasion across tested Windows and macOS lab configurations, including macOS 26 where the attack was previously assumed mitigated. Configurations were simulated, not commercial proctoring products; macOS 26 used native CGWindowListCreateImage and screencapture rather than browser getDisplayMedia(), and Linux was not tested. Findings reflect the tested software versions as of March 2026 and may change after patches.
claim_checks.status: supported as reported/configured at pinned source; no project execution performed

claim_checks.value: Remote proctoring systems detect prohibited content by capturing the student's screen via the WebRTC getDisplayMedia() API. The implicit security assumption is that the captured frame faithfully represents the physical display. The research demonstrates a gap in that assumption: documented OS display APIs excluded windows in tested capture paths without privilege escalation or kernel modification. These findings concern controlled, simulated Windows and macOS configurations; they do not establish bypass of every browser or commercial proctoring product.
